facts.text: MPC (8-9 Apr) kept all NBP rates unchanged, in line with expectations: reference 3.75%, lombard 4.25%, deposit 3.25%, rediscount 3.80%, discount 3.85%. Statement at 15:00, Glapinski conference 15:00.

MPC statement: further decisions depend on incoming information on inflation and activity prospects, currently affected by changes in commodity prices and global inflation in the geopolitical context; CPI risks also include fiscal policy and fuel-price regulation, activity and wage dynamics; NBP may intervene in the FX market; global outlook highly uncertain.

Post-conference views: ING - neutral tone, rates unchanged to year-end; Millennium - rates unchanged at least to July, base case to year-end, return to cuts unlikely; Bank Pocztowy (Kurtek) - a cut at year-end possible if oil normalises, hikes possible if the conflict persists.

ING BSK: CPN may stay until end-July; 2026 average CPI 3.2% (vs ~2% pre-war); ceasefire need not mean a quick fall in oil and gas prices.

digest.2026-04-01: 31 Mar: March flash CPI 3.0% y/y (1.0% m/m) vs 3.3% expected, with fuels +15.4% m/m and food flat; MoF's April plan: sales on 15 Apr (PLN 4-12bn), 23 Apr (6-14bn) and 28 Apr (5-13bn, new DS0436 from 23 Apr), no switch, a 10 Apr 50-week T-bill (3-6bn); Q2 plan 7-8 sales for 50-90bn plus 1-2 switches; non-residents bought PLN 7.0bn of POLGBs in February (12.7% share); BGK sees NBP rates flat in 2026; POLGB yields fell 6-8bp intraday after the 10Y neared 6% on 30 Mar.
digest.2026-04-02: 1 Apr: POLGB yields fell by double digits across the curve on de-escalation hopes and the soft CPI, with the market removing part of the NBP hike pricing (ING); GUS: 2025 GG deficit 7.2% of GDP, debt 59.7%; the Fiscal Council warned that extending the fuel package to end-2026 would add 0.37% of GDP to the deficit and probably force a budget amendment; NBP forecaster survey: 2026 CPI 2.9%, no rate change this year; March manufacturing PMI rose to 48.7 from 47.1 (Millennium had forecast 47.6).
digest.2026-04-07: 2-6 Apr: MPC's Kotecki said the March cut was the last this year and Litwiniuk ruled out near-term cuts, with hikes possible if inflation worsens (2 Apr); S&P raised its 2026 deficit forecast for Poland to 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); POLGB yields rose only 1-3bp on 2 Apr after Trump's escalatory speech; FRAs priced ~50bp of 2026 NBP hikes (PKO); no bond sessions on 3 and 6 Apr; MPC decides on Thu 9 Apr; 2026 borrowing needs ~41% financed at end-Q1.
digest.2026-04-08: 7 Apr: MoF mandated four banks and priced USD 6bn of 5Y, 10Y and 30Y bonds (yields 4.645%, 5.405%, 6.233%; UST +65/+105/+130bp); POLGB yields edged higher ahead of Trump's Iran deadline; Millennium: markets price two NBP hikes (50bp) within a year; PKO expects no rate change this year and the market to unwind hike bets after the MPC; NBP reserves fell to EUR 253.5bn in March on gold valuation; Credit Agricole sees the fuel package possibly lasting to Feb 2027 and rates at 3.75%.
digest.2026-04-09: 8 Apr: after the two-week US-Iran ceasefire POLGB yields fell ~40bp across the curve, and FRAs went from pricing up to three 2026 NBP hikes to at most one (PKO); PAP survey: the MPC holds 3.75% on 9 Apr and through H1 2027, one cut in H2 2027; MoF said demand for its USD 6bn issue confirmed investor confidence; March retail bond sales PLN 7.27bn; PM Tusk keeps the CPN fuel package; Domanski: windfall-tax bill for fuel firms in April; World Bank cut Poland's 2026 GDP forecast to 3.1%.
digest.2026-04-10: 9 Apr: the MPC kept the reference rate at 3.75% as expected; its statement names commodity prices, fiscal policy and fuel-price regulation as CPI risks; Glapinski sees no near-term change either way, hikes only in a 'black scenario' of renewed war and a question mark over cuts; NBP's 2025 loss was PLN 35.7bn; MoF: budget accounts PLN 169.5bn at end-March, domestic debt maturity 4.18 years; yields rose slightly after the decision; ING expects the fuel package to run to end-July and 2026 CPI of 3.2%.
digest.2026-04-13: 10-12 Apr: MoF sold PLN 3.005bn of a new 50-week T-bill (Mar 2027) at 3.95% on 3.605bn demand (offer 3-6bn) plus 0.394bn additional; Domanski: the war's impact is limited, no budget amendment needed, and the fuel-excise cut stays after 15 Apr; PKO sees MoF issuance plans safe and new supply neutral; Santander sees the 10Y POLGB near 5.5% and NBP rates flat in 2026-27; yields fell with core markets on 10 Apr; NBP put its unrealised gold gain at PLN 169bn.
digest.2026-04-14: 13 Apr: MoF set the 15 Apr sale at PLN 6-12bn (plan floor 4bn) in OK0128, WS0428, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1035 and NZ0936, and extended the fuel-excise cut to 30 Apr (VAT cut also to 30 Apr); March MPC minutes: most members saw a much lower chance of further cuts; February C/A -EUR 990m vs +434m expected; Janczyk: rates flat for coming quarters; unemployment 6.1% (6.0% expected); yields edged up after the failed US-Iran talks; Millennium: ~one 2026 hike priced.
digest.2026-04-15: 14 Apr: the budget deficit after March was ~PLN 69.5bn, 25.6% of the 271.7bn annual limit (MoF); Kotecki: keep rates unchanged at least until the July projection, but the MPC would act without hesitation either way; Janczyk (via PKO): hikes only if CPI stays above 3.75% for three months; BGK offers FPC bonds (min PLN 0.5bn) on 16 Apr; the IMF sees 2026 GDP 3.3% and CPI 3.3%; the 10Y POLGB held near 5.52% ahead of Wednesday's 6-12bn sale; ING called the T-bill auction disappointing.
